podcast.title: Consideration of a "Beatles Offspring" Band
podcast.body: Zach Starkey was friends with James McCartney, Danny Harrison, and Sean Lennon, and they explored the idea of forming a band together, although it never materialized. "He eventually became friends with Danny Harrison, son of George, Zach Starky, son of Ringo, and Sean Lennon, son of John. They floored with the idea of forming their own band. Imagine that, but nothing ever came of it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Father's Discouragement and Early Bands
podcast.body: His father, Ringo Starr, gave him only one drum lesson and attempted to discourage him from a career in show business, advising him to be a doctor or lawyer instead of a musician. Despite this, Zach first joined a garage band called The Next, then a reformed version of the Spencer Davis Group. "Dad gave him exactly one lesson before he tried to dissuade his son about getting into show business. Be a doctor, be a lawyer, don't be a musician. Yeah, that didn't work. First came a garage band called The Next. Then he ended up in a reformed version of the Spencer Davis group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Godfather and First Drum Kit
podcast.body: Zach Starkey, son of Ringo Starr and Maureen, received his first drum kit from his godfather, Keith Moon of The Who. "Just like dad, he plays drums. He got his first kit from Keith Moon of the Who, who was also his godfather."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Oasis Tenure
podcast.body: In 2004, Zach Starkey joined Oasis as an employee rather than a full member, a status he preferred as it allowed him the flexibility to pursue other projects when not needed by Oasis. He recorded his first album with them, *Don't Believe the Truth*, in 2005, which included the song "Lyla." "In 2004, he joined Oasis. Zach was with them as an employee, not actually a member of the band, but he liked it that way because it allowed him to go into his own things when he wasn't needed with Oasis. So here's Zach. On the first album, he recorded with Oasis. It's from Don't Believe the Truth from 2005 and Lila."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Working with Father and The Who
podcast.body: Eventually, Ringo Starr relented and had Zach work with his own band. Zach also secured a gig with The Who and has been their on-call drummer for live performances ever since. "His dad then gave up and had him work with his band. He got a gig with The Who, which seems fitting, given his family history. And since then, he's been on call with them whenever the Who plays live."

xref.body: James McCartney has appeared on albums by both his father, Paul McCartney, and his mother, Linda McCartney. He became friends with other Beatles offspring—Danny Harrison, Zach Starkey, and Sean Lennon—and they entertained the idea of forming a band, though it didn't come to fruition. "He's appeared on albums by both Paul and Linda and has several records of his own. He eventually became friends with Danny Harrison, son of George, Zach Starky, son of Ringo, and Sean Lennon, son of John. They floored with the idea of forming their own band. Imagine that, but nothing ever came of it."
